newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Goldman sees possible Swedish monetary tightening.
newsitem.headline: Goldman sees possible Swedish monetary tightening.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs said on Wednesday that the current weak Swedish crown could oblige the country's central bank to raise rates.
The Goldman Sachs report, which dented the crown further and pushed up bond yields, saw the crown at 4.50 per mark in six months time and slightly weaker in 12 months, at 4.55.
"Sweden probably needs to tighten monetary policy to prevent a significant crown decline," it said.
The crown had softened to 4.5200 against the mark on Wednesday, from 4.2995 about five months ago.

The decline is attributed to the strong dollar, doubts about the timetable for economic and monetary union and to fears of increased spending by Sweden's increasingly unpopular government ahead of 1998 elections.
The central bank's key repo rate currently stands at 4.10 percent. It has not been moved so far in 1997, but was steadily cut throughout 1996 from 8.91 percent.
